summary: Defines the Network Control Protocol for establishing and configuring DECnet Phase IV routing over PPP. It applies only to DNA Phase IV routing messages. It was replaced by RFC 1762.

eli5.summary: When two old Digital company computers connect over PPP, this lets them agree on how to carry their special kind of network messages.

questions: how does decnet work over ppp
subtitle: How to run DECnet Phase IV routing over PPP links

tldr.problem: DECnet Phase IV is a networking system used by Digital computers, originally designed for Ethernet links. Point-to-point connections (PPP) need a way to carry DECnet routing messages.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the DECnet Phase IV Network Control Protocol (DNCP), which negotiates and configures DECnet Phase IV routing over PPP links. DNCP follows the same exchange mechanism as the PPP Link Control Protocol, allowing both endpoints to agree on parameters before routing traffic begins.
tldr.outcome: DECnet networks can use PPP for serial links and point-to-point connections, extending connectivity beyond Ethernet. However, this RFC was replaced by RFC 1762 with updated specifications.

today: RFC 1376 specified how to carry DECnet Phase IV routing over PPP but is now obsolete. It was replaced by RFC 1762 with updated specifications.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
DECnet Phase IV is a networking system developed by Digital Equipment Corporation. Originally, DECnet routers communicated over Ethernet and other broadcast media using the same data and control messages. However, to extend DECnet networks over point-to-point serial links, a different approach was needed.

RFC 1376 takes the first approach: treating the PPP serial link as if it were an Ethernet link, but using the PPP encapsulation. It defines the DECnet Phase IV Network Control Protocol (DNCP), which operates within the PPP framework. DNCP is responsible for configuring the DECnet Phase IV routing protocol module on both ends of a PPP link before any routing data is exchanged.
sections.eli5: DECnet is the way old Digital computers talk to each other. When they connect over a phone line using PPP, they need to agree on how to communicate. This document explains that negotiation process.

sections.title: Phase IV DNA Protocols
sections.content:
Phase IV Digital Network Architecture includes several protocols that operate over data links. DECnet Phase IV Routing is the network layer protocol that routes messages between DECnet nodes, similar to the role of IP in the Internet. Other Phase IV protocols include the DNA System Console (for maintenance and diagnostics), the DNA Naming Service and Time Service (for distributed database and clock synchronization), DNA Load/Dump (for remote system administration), and others.

This RFC specifically addresses DECnet Phase IV Routing, which is the data-carrying protocol. It does not cover the other DNA protocols, though a separate NCP could be defined for each. The DNCP enables only the routing protocol to operate over PPP; other DNA services would require their own negotiation protocols.
sections.eli5: DECnet includes many services: routing, naming, timing, maintenance, and more. This document only explains how to carry routing messages over PPP; the other services are separate.

sections.title: The DECnet Phase IV Network Control Protocol
sections.content:
The DNCP follows the same packet exchange mechanism as the PPP Link Control Protocol (LCP). Like LCP, DNCP can only begin exchanging packets after PPP reaches the Network-Layer Protocol phase, following successful link establishment and optional authentication.

The protocol uses six message types from the LCP family: Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject, Terminate-Request, and Terminate-Ack. Code-Reject messages are also supported for unrecognized codes. Unlike LCP, DNCP has no configuration options: the two ends simply negotiate whether DECnet Phase IV routing is enabled on the link.
sections.eli5: DNCP is a simple negotiation protocol. Each endpoint sends messages saying 'I want to use DECnet routing' and the other side says 'OK' or 'Not now', just like two people shaking hands to agree on a conversation.

sections.title: Encapsulating DECnet Packets
sections.content:
Once DNCP reaches the Opened state, DECnet Phase IV routing packets can be transmitted. Each packet is encapsulated with a two-octet length field (in VAX byte ordering, with least significant byte first) followed by the DECnet Phase IV Routing packet itself. This length field is needed to disambiguate optional padding octets from actual packet data.

The protocol type in the PPP header for DNCP control packets is hex 8027 (DECnet Phase IV Control Protocol), while DNCP data packets use type hex 0027 (DECnet Phase IV Routing). The packet format is identical to DECnet over Ethernet, except that the Ethernet header, padding, and frame check sequence fields are omitted. The maximum packet length is limited by the PPP link's maximum information field size, minus two octets for the length field.
sections.eli5: When sending DECnet messages over PPP, each message is wrapped with a length tag (so the receiver knows where one message ends and padding begins) and given a special label so PPP knows what kind of message it is.

sections.title: Routing Behavior and Timers
sections.content:
DECnet Phase IV routing behavior differs depending on the underlying medium. Over guaranteed-delivery links like DDCMP (Digital's serial protocol), routers can use longer retransmit times (600 seconds) because packet loss is rare. Over PPP, where some packet loss may occur, administrators should configure shorter retransmit intervals to detect topology changes quickly. The interval between routing updates should be user-configurable per interface and based on the error rate of the underlying link.

The RFC recommends using broadcast-link timers for PPP: a 15-second Hello timer and a 45-second Listen timer. If the remote node is an endnode (not a router), the local router does not need to send routing updates; endnodes must discard any routing updates received over PPP. The node type can be determined from hello messages exchanged during the protocol negotiation phase.
sections.eli5: DECnet routers periodically send updates about the network topology. On reliable links, they can wait longer between updates. On PPP, they should send more frequently so changes are noticed quickly. The exact timing is up to the administrator.
